text:
Sam W: paging on-call — we're seeing sustained queue depth rise on the 'generation' pool, customers hitting throttles :rotating_light:
Priya K: saw the incident bot: `INCIDENT #2201` automated page fired at 1918765420 — queue_depth > 1200 for 5m
oncall-bot: :bell: Page: @oncall Rotation (Sam W) — Rule: gen_pool_queue_depth_high — severity: P1
Sam W: I'm on it, joining from home, starting mitigation checklist
Jordan L: +1 I'm looking at telemetry now, tokens/sec spiked then dropped off — looks like a traffic shaping event from one tenant
Marta_R: customer-impact check: support reports 3 customers complaining of 429s, one customer (acme-corp) reported degraded throughput for webhooks
Sam W: reading metrics — queue depth hit 1734 at peak, throttle_events spiked to 412 in 10m. tokens/sec per-node dropped ~40% as many requests retried
Priya K: can we throttle that noisy tenant? We have routing policies that can temporarily cap QPS per-tenant.
Sam W: initiating temporary rate-limit for tenant `acme-batch-sender` to 30r/s via infra-ops runbook now
infra-ops: applied temporary policy: `route: tenant=acme-batch-sender cap=30/s` — changes propagated to edge in ~30s
Jordan L: adding a short-lived autoscale burst to gen-pool, requested +2 workers, ETA ~90s
Marta_R: on the support side I'm notifying the affected customers (acme, beta-co, devsquad) — message: "We're aware, mitigation in progress. Expect partial recovery in <5m."
Sam W: good. Observing queue depth starting to decline after rate-limit, current = 860
Priya K: we still got a lot of alert noise from the queue_depth rule, dozens of pages last night during transient spikes — we need better squelch/hysteresis
Jordan L: agree. Current rule: alert when queue_depth > 1000 for 5m. That dog-walks on bursts. Proposed: require both queue_depth > 1200 and throttle_events > 50 in 5m to page.
Marta_R: and add tokens/sec drop as secondary signal? e.g., tokens_per_sec < 0.7*baseline to indicate throughput degradation
Sam W: draft rule I propose:
```
name: gen_pool_intervention
conditions:
  - queue_depth > 1200 for 5m
  - throttle_events > 50 for 5m
  - tokens_per_sec < baseline*0.75 for 10m (or absent)
severity: P1
runbook: notify on-call, apply tenant cap, add autoscale burst, follow post-incident review
```
Priya K: I like that. Also recommend adding a transient suppression window: if queue_depth spikes but clears below 800 within 3m, do NOT page (auto-squelch)
Jordan L: implementation detail: our alerting backend supports composite rules with 'AND' and 'recovery window' — I can author the MQL for that. Will also attach a small suppressor: count(queue_depth > 1200) over 5m >=1 AND not existed(queue_depth < 800 within 3m)
infra-ops: created alert PR: https://git.internal/rules/234 — please review
Sam W: note for runbook: prefer tenant cap + autoscale burst over global throttles. Global throttle causes collateral impact for low-latency customers.
Marta_R: added a line to support templates to ask affected customers whether they saw 429s or latency. That helps triage in future incidents.
Priya K: dashboard work: need a compact panel that shows queue_depth, throttle_events, tokens/sec, and top-5 tenant QPS. Can we add it to the gen-pool dashboard and the 1-click incident view?
Jordan L: I'll add the panel. Query suggestions:
- queue_depth: sum(queue_depth) by pool
- throttle_events: derivative(count(throttle), 5m)
- tokens/sec: sum(tokens_processed)/interval
- top tenants: topk(5, sum(qps) by tenant)
Sam W: while we're adjusting alerts let's also change notification channels: P1 pages to oncall + #eng-sre-incident in addition to email. And suppress paging for P2s to slack-only.
Priya K: action items from this thread:
- Jordan: codify composite alert and create PR (owner) — due EOD
- Jordan: add dashboard panel + incident view snippet (owner) — due tomorrow
- Priya: update alerting runbook text about hysteresis and transient suppression (owner) — due EOD
- Sam: follow up with infra-ops on reserving +2 burst capacity for gen-pool during peak windows (owner) — due next week
- Marta: update customer templates and notify affected customers (owner) — in flight
infra-ops: autoscale burst succeeded, +2 workers added, capacity now stable
Sam W: queue_depth now 410, throttle_events dropping — looks like recovery. Leaving page open until we validate 30m stability
Jordan L: will instrument a short-lived anomaly detector to flag noisy tenants earlier — prototype will emit a low-severity alert (no page) to #eng-sre for 2 weeks
Priya K: follow-up proposal for post-incident review: run a small bakeoff to choose thresholds. We'll collect 14 days of baseline metrics and evaluate false positive vs detection latency tradeoff. Recommend using ROC-style analysis across thresholds.
Marta_R: can we tag incidents with customer-impact = {none, partial, degraded, outage} in the incident bot? I flagged this one as 'partial' in the ticket. That would help prioritize communications.
Sam W: agreed. Good note for postmortem. For now I'll silence the gen_pool_queue_depth_old rule for 48h to avoid duplicate noise while we iterate on the new composite rule
Jordan L: PR updated to include suppression and dashboard link: https://git.internal/rules/234 (diff attached). Requesting reviews from @Priya K and @Sam W
Priya K: reviewed and left comments on threshold math. small nit: use median baseline not mean to avoid skew from outliers
Sam W: ack. Great response everyone — closing the active page in 10m if stable. We'll do a short post-incident doc in #postmortems with action items and timelines. :thumbsup:
